questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of Religious Education in Grade 9?
options: To deepen faith knowledge and apply values to responsible living
To replace science and social studies in school
To rank learners according to their religion
To avoid discussing moral choices
questions.correctAnswer: To deepen faith knowledge and apply values to responsible living
questions.explanation: Religious Education helps learners understand beliefs, values, worship, service, and moral responsibility in daily life.
questions.strandTitle: Foundations of Faith and Moral Identity
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how Religious Education supports personal growth and responsible citizenship.

questions.prompt: Which value is shown when a learner keeps a promise even when no one is checking?
options: Integrity
Pride
Jealousy
Carelessness
questions.correctAnswer: Integrity
questions.explanation: Integrity means being honest and morally consistent in both public and private actions.
questions.strandTitle: Foundations of Faith and Moral Identity
questions.learningOutcome: Identify values that guide trustworthy conduct in school and community life.

questions.prompt: What is conscience in moral decision making?
options: The inner ability to judge right and wrong before acting
A rule that removes personal responsibility
A way of copying friends without thinking
The habit of avoiding every difficult choice
questions.correctAnswer: The inner ability to judge right and wrong before acting
questions.explanation: Conscience helps a person reflect on values, duties, and consequences before choosing an action.
questions.strandTitle: Foundations of Faith and Moral Identity
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the role of conscience in making responsible choices.

questions.prompt: A learner refuses to spread a rumour about a classmate. Which value is being applied most directly?
options: Respect for truth and dignity
Desire for revenge
Fear of learning
Love of gossip
questions.correctAnswer: Respect for truth and dignity
questions.explanation: Refusing rumours protects truth and the dignity of the person who could be harmed.
questions.strandTitle: Foundations of Faith and Moral Identity
questions.learningOutcome: Apply religious values to speech that protects truth and human dignity.

questions.prompt: Why is self-examination important in religious and moral growth?
options: It helps a person notice faults and choose improvement
It gives permission to blame others for everything
It makes correction unnecessary
It proves that a learner cannot change
questions.correctAnswer: It helps a person notice faults and choose improvement
questions.explanation: Self-examination supports repentance, humility, and better choices after honest reflection.
questions.strandTitle: Foundations of Faith and Moral Identity
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how reflection supports repentance and personal improvement.

questions.prompt: Which action best shows humility during a discussion about religion?
options: Listening carefully and accepting that one can learn from others
Interrupting everyone to prove superiority
Mocking beliefs that are unfamiliar
Refusing to answer respectful questions
questions.correctAnswer: Listening carefully and accepting that one can learn from others
questions.explanation: Humility allows learners to listen, ask honestly, and speak without disrespecting others.
questions.strandTitle: Foundations of Faith and Moral Identity
questions.learningOutcome: Demonstrate humility and respect when discussing religious beliefs.

questions.prompt: A learner finds two possible actions: one is easy but dishonest, the other is hard but truthful. What should guide the choice?
options: Values, conscience, consequences, and trusted guidance
The easiest path only
What hides the facts best
The loudest friend's opinion
questions.correctAnswer: Values, conscience, consequences, and trusted guidance
questions.explanation: Responsible decisions consider moral values, facts, likely effects, and wise guidance before acting.
questions.strandTitle: Foundations of Faith and Moral Identity
questions.learningOutcome: Use a responsible process to choose between competing moral options.

questions.prompt: Which situation most clearly requires moral courage?
options: Refusing to join friends who plan to cheat in an assessment
Joining a club clean-up activity
Borrowing a library book with permission
Greeting visitors politely
questions.correctAnswer: Refusing to join friends who plan to cheat in an assessment
questions.explanation: Moral courage is needed when doing what is right may lead to pressure, ridicule, or loss of approval.
questions.strandTitle: Foundations of Faith and Moral Identity
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize situations that require courage to uphold moral values.

questions.prompt: Which question best helps a learner analyse whether an action respects religious values?
options: Does it protect truth, dignity, justice, and responsibility?
Will it make me look powerful?
Can I hide it from adults?
Will it help me avoid every duty?
questions.correctAnswer: Does it protect truth, dignity, justice, and responsibility?
questions.explanation: A values-based question checks whether the action respects people and supports moral responsibility.
questions.strandTitle: Foundations of Faith and Moral Identity
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze moral choices using religious values and likely consequences.

questions.prompt: A class is writing a values pledge for Grade 9. Which statement is most suitable?
options: We will seek truth, respect dignity, repair harm, and serve others responsibly
We will ignore anyone who disagrees with us
We will hide mistakes to protect our image
We will copy work whenever tasks are difficult
questions.correctAnswer: We will seek truth, respect dignity, repair harm, and serve others responsibly
questions.explanation: A strong pledge names practical values that guide conduct, relationships, and accountability.
questions.strandTitle: Foundations of Faith and Moral Identity
questions.learningOutcome: Create practical commitments that apply religious values in school life.

questions.prompt: Which sacred text is central to Christian worship and teaching?
options: The Bible
The Quran
The Vedas
A school atlas
questions.correctAnswer: The Bible
questions.explanation: Christians use the Bible for worship, teaching, prayer, and moral guidance.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify sacred texts used in selected religious traditions.

questions.prompt: Which sacred text do Muslims regard as the revealed word of God?
options: The Quran
The Bible
The Bhagavad Gita
The Tripitaka
questions.correctAnswer: The Quran
questions.explanation: The Quran is central to Islamic belief, worship, and guidance for daily conduct.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify sacred texts used in selected religious traditions.

questions.prompt: What is the Hadith in Islamic tradition?
options: Reports about the sayings and actions of Prophet Muhammad
A collection of weather records
A type of school timetable
A map of trade routes
questions.correctAnswer: Reports about the sayings and actions of Prophet Muhammad
questions.explanation: Hadith helps Muslims understand the Prophet's example and apply Islamic teachings responsibly.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe sources of guidance used in Islamic tradition.

questions.prompt: Which Hindu text is well known for teaching about duty, devotion, and wisdom through dialogue?
options: The Bhagavad Gita
The Gospel of Luke
The Hadith
The Psalms
questions.correctAnswer: The Bhagavad Gita
questions.explanation: The Bhagavad Gita presents teachings on duty, devotion, self-control, and spiritual understanding.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify examples of sacred writings in selected traditions.

questions.prompt: Why should learners consider context when reading a short quotation from a sacred text?
options: Context helps them understand the intended meaning more accurately
Context allows them to change the words freely
Context makes every interpretation unnecessary
Context is useful only in mathematics
questions.correctAnswer: Context helps them understand the intended meaning more accurately
questions.explanation: Reading the surrounding message and asking knowledgeable guidance reduces misunderstanding and misuse.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain why context matters when interpreting religious teachings.

questions.prompt: A learner compares teachings on generosity from two religions. Which method is most respectful?
options: Identify each teaching, note shared values, and describe differences fairly
Choose one religion to mock
Read only the shortest sentence
Rank classmates by their faith
questions.correctAnswer: Identify each teaching, note shared values, and describe differences fairly
questions.explanation: Respectful comparison builds understanding without ridicule or unfair ranking.
questions.learningOutcome: Compare moral teachings from different traditions respectfully.

questions.prompt: Which conclusion is reasonable after studying teachings about honesty in several faith traditions?
options: Many religions encourage truthfulness because it builds trust
Honesty matters only when teachers are present
Religions reject truthfulness in daily life
Truthfulness is useful only in business lessons
questions.correctAnswer: Many religions encourage truthfulness because it builds trust
questions.explanation: Religious teachings often support honest conduct because trust protects relationships and dignity.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain shared moral values found in selected religious teachings.

questions.prompt: Which response shows responsible interpretation of a religious teaching that seems difficult?
options: Study the passage, ask a trusted teacher, and consider the wider teaching
Use the sentence immediately to insult others
Ignore all explanation from knowledgeable people
Change the words to fit a personal opinion
questions.correctAnswer: Study the passage, ask a trusted teacher, and consider the wider teaching
questions.explanation: Responsible interpretation uses context, guidance, and reflection before applying a teaching.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze ways to interpret sacred teachings responsibly.

questions.prompt: Which question would best help evaluate whether a religious story has been applied well?
options: Did the action reflect the value taught and protect people's dignity?
Did the learner repeat the story title only?
Did the action embarrass the weakest person?
Did the learner avoid every real-life connection?
questions.correctAnswer: Did the action reflect the value taught and protect people's dignity?
questions.explanation: Application is strong when the learner connects the teaching to conduct that respects values and people.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate how religious teachings are applied to everyday conduct.

questions.prompt: A group is preparing a presentation on forgiveness in sacred texts. Which plan is strongest?
options: Use accurate sources, explain the value, give examples, and suggest peaceful actions
Use rumours and avoid naming any value
Copy long paragraphs without understanding
Turn the presentation into a contest between religions
questions.correctAnswer: Use accurate sources, explain the value, give examples, and suggest peaceful actions
questions.explanation: A good presentation combines accuracy, meaning, examples, and responsible application.
questions.learningOutcome: Create accurate presentations that connect sacred teachings with moral action.

questions.prompt: What is prayer in many religious traditions?
options: Communication with God or a spiritual reality
A method for measuring rainfall
A way of avoiding all duties
A school punishment
questions.correctAnswer: Communication with God or a spiritual reality
questions.explanation: Prayer is commonly understood as worshipful communication that may include praise, thanks, confession, or request.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the meaning and purpose of prayer in religious life.

questions.prompt: Which practice is the regular ritual prayer performed by Muslims at set times?
options: Salah
Baptism
Diwali
Eucharist
questions.correctAnswer: Salah
questions.explanation: Salah is a central Islamic act of worship performed regularly as obedience to God.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify selected forms of worship in different faith traditions.

questions.prompt: Which action best shows respect during a visit to a place of worship?
options: Following expected conduct and asking before touching sacred items
Laughing at unfamiliar practices
Interrupting worship to take photos
Using the visit to argue loudly
questions.correctAnswer: Following expected conduct and asking before touching sacred items
questions.explanation: Respect includes observing customs, protecting sacred space, and avoiding disruption.
questions.learningOutcome: Demonstrate respectful behavior in places of worship.

questions.prompt: Why do many faith communities gather for worship?
options: To express faith, receive guidance, and strengthen community bonds
To avoid all moral responsibility
To compete over who is richest
To stop learners from studying
questions.correctAnswer: To express faith, receive guidance, and strengthen community bonds
questions.explanation: Communal worship often supports shared belief, teaching, service, encouragement, and belonging.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the role of communal worship in religious life.

questions.prompt: Which statement best compares personal and communal prayer?
options: Personal prayer is individual, while communal prayer is shared with others
Personal prayer must always be noisy, while communal prayer must be silent
Personal prayer replaces every duty, while communal prayer removes values
Both are only school activities
questions.correctAnswer: Personal prayer is individual, while communal prayer is shared with others
questions.explanation: Both forms can be meaningful, but they differ in whether a person prays alone or with a group.
questions.learningOutcome: Compare personal and communal forms of prayer respectfully.

questions.prompt: A learner wants to interview a religious leader about worship. Which question is most appropriate?
options: What values does this worship practice teach believers?
Why should everyone abandon their religion?
Which group should be mocked most?
Can I interrupt prayers for entertainment?
questions.correctAnswer: What values does this worship practice teach believers?
questions.explanation: A respectful question seeks understanding and connects practice with meaning and values.
questions.learningOutcome: Use respectful inquiry to learn about worship practices.

questions.prompt: Which festival is commonly associated with the Hindu celebration of light over darkness?
options: Diwali
Eid al-Fitr
Christmas
Ash Wednesday
questions.correctAnswer: Diwali
questions.explanation: Diwali is widely associated with light, renewal, worship, family sharing, and moral reflection in Hindu communities.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify selected religious festivals and their meanings.

questions.prompt: Which question best helps analyse a religious festival beyond its outward activities?
options: What belief, value, or memory does the festival express?
How many decorations can be counted?
Which food is easiest to copy?
How can visitors ignore the meaning?
questions.correctAnswer: What belief, value, or memory does the festival express?
questions.explanation: Analysis looks beyond visible activities to the beliefs, values, and historical memories they carry.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze the values and beliefs expressed through religious festivals.

questions.prompt: A school plans to host learners from several faiths for a worship-site learning visit. Which guideline is most important?
options: Seek permission, learn expected conduct, and protect every participant's dignity
Let learners enter anywhere without guidance
Ask learners to mock customs they do not follow
Turn the visit into a competition between religions
questions.correctAnswer: Seek permission, learn expected conduct, and protect every participant's dignity
questions.explanation: Careful preparation helps learners observe respectfully and learn without disrupting worship or offending others.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze requirements for respectful learning visits to places of worship.

questions.prompt: Which activity would best help Grade 9 learners connect worship with service?
options: Plan a community support activity after reflecting on teachings about compassion
Attend worship then ignore people in need
Collect donations without records
Use worship time to spread rumours
questions.correctAnswer: Plan a community support activity after reflecting on teachings about compassion
questions.explanation: Worship is meaningfully connected to life when values such as compassion become practical service.
questions.learningOutcome: Create service activities inspired by worship and religious values.

questions.prompt: In Christian teaching, what does creation mainly refer to?
options: God's bringing the universe and life into being
A school rule about uniforms
A market plan for selling goods
A road map of Kenya
questions.correctAnswer: God's bringing the universe and life into being
questions.explanation: Christian teaching links creation with God's power, purpose, human dignity, and stewardship.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe Christian teaching on creation and human responsibility.

questions.prompt: What does vocation mean in Christian Religious Education?
options: A calling to serve God and society through one's work and gifts
A way to avoid work
A punishment given at school
A list of market prices
questions.correctAnswer: A calling to serve God and society through one's work and gifts
questions.explanation: Vocation connects work, talents, service, responsibility, and a sense of calling.
questions.learningOutcome: Define vocation as a call to responsible service through work.

questions.prompt: Which Christian value is shown when work is done honestly without exploiting others?
options: Justice
Greed
Deceit
Laziness
questions.correctAnswer: Justice
questions.explanation: Justice in work includes fairness, honest effort, respect for others, and responsible use of resources.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain Christian values that guide honest and fair work.

questions.prompt: Which action best applies the Parable of the Good Samaritan to school life?
options: Helping an injured learner and seeking adult support
Passing by a learner in distress
Mocking someone who needs help
Helping only when a reward is promised
questions.correctAnswer: Helping an injured learner and seeking adult support
questions.explanation: The parable teaches compassion that crosses barriers and responds to real need.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply Jesus' teachings on compassion to everyday situations.

questions.prompt: Which statement best explains why Christians study the Bible with guidance?
options: Guidance helps them understand context, message, and application
Guidance allows them to ignore the text
Guidance means changing every teaching
Guidance makes worship unnecessary
questions.correctAnswer: Guidance helps them understand context, message, and application
questions.explanation: Bible study is stronger when learners consider context, teaching, and responsible application.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how guided Bible study supports responsible interpretation.

questions.prompt: A learner wants to practise Christian stewardship at home. Which choice is best?
options: Saving water, avoiding waste, and caring for shared property
Damaging property to impress friends
Leaving taps open because water is available
Throwing litter into drainage channels
questions.correctAnswer: Saving water, avoiding waste, and caring for shared property
questions.explanation: Stewardship means caring responsibly for creation and resources entrusted to people.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply Christian stewardship to household and community resources.

questions.prompt: Which example best shows forgiveness joined with accountability?
options: Accepting an apology while agreeing on how the harm will be repaired
Pretending harm never happened
Demanding revenge beyond the harm caused
Refusing every peaceful discussion
questions.correctAnswer: Accepting an apology while agreeing on how the harm will be repaired
questions.explanation: Christian teaching on forgiveness can restore relationships while still supporting truth and repair.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply forgiveness and accountability in restoring relationships.

questions.prompt: Which question best analyses whether a Christian response to poverty is responsible?
options: Does it protect dignity, meet real needs, and encourage accountability?
Does it shame people in need?
Does it collect resources without records?
Does it help only people who can repay immediately?
questions.correctAnswer: Does it protect dignity, meet real needs, and encourage accountability?
questions.explanation: Responsible service should be compassionate, fair, transparent, and respectful of human dignity.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze service activities using Christian values of compassion and justice.

questions.prompt: A Bible discussion group has two different views about a passage. Which response is most mature?
options: Listen respectfully, review the context, and seek informed guidance
Insult the learner with a different view
Stop reading the passage completely
Choose the view that sounds easiest
questions.correctAnswer: Listen respectfully, review the context, and seek informed guidance
questions.explanation: Mature discussion combines respect, careful reading, humility, and guidance.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze respectful ways of handling different interpretations.

questions.prompt: Which plan best helps a Grade 9 Christian group promote honest work in school?
options: Create a pledge, model original work, support revision, and report cheating fairly
Hide cheating if friends are involved
Mock learners who struggle academically
Copy assignments but promise to stop later
questions.correctAnswer: Create a pledge, model original work, support revision, and report cheating fairly
questions.explanation: A strong plan combines values, example, support, and fair accountability.
questions.learningOutcome: Create practical strategies for promoting honest work and responsibility.

questions.prompt: In Islam, what does Tawhid teach?
options: The oneness of Allah
The worship of many gods
The rejection of prayer
The ownership of all wealth by one person
questions.correctAnswer: The oneness of Allah
questions.explanation: Tawhid is the central Islamic belief that Allah is one and deserves worship.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify key Islamic beliefs related to faith in Allah.

questions.prompt: Which Islamic practice involves giving a required share to support people in need?
options: Zakat
Hajj
Salah
Tawhid
questions.correctAnswer: Zakat
questions.explanation: Zakat is required giving that supports social responsibility, purification, and care for vulnerable people.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify devotional acts that promote obedience and social responsibility.

questions.prompt: What is Sawm during Ramadan mainly meant to develop?
options: Self-control, God-consciousness, and compassion
Careless eating
Avoidance of all prayer
Pride over people who are poor
questions.correctAnswer: Self-control, God-consciousness, and compassion
questions.explanation: Fasting teaches discipline, awareness of Allah, gratitude, and concern for those in need.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain values developed through fasting in Islam.

questions.prompt: Which action best reflects the Islamic value of amanah?
options: Keeping a trust and returning borrowed property safely
Using another person's property without permission
Breaking a promise deliberately
Hiding resources meant for a group
questions.correctAnswer: Keeping a trust and returning borrowed property safely
questions.explanation: Amanah refers to trustworthiness and responsible care for what one has been entrusted with.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply Islamic moral values to trust and responsibility.

questions.prompt: Which statement best explains why Muslims study both Quran and Hadith?
options: The Quran gives revelation and Hadith helps explain the Prophet's example
Hadith replaces all prayer
The Quran is used only for decoration
Both are unrelated to daily conduct
questions.correctAnswer: The Quran gives revelation and Hadith helps explain the Prophet's example
questions.explanation: Together, Quran and Hadith guide belief, worship, character, and practical conduct.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how Quran and Hadith guide Islamic belief and conduct.

questions.prompt: A learner is tempted to exaggerate marks to impress friends. Which Islamic value should guide the learner?
options: Sidq, or truthfulness
Israf, or wastefulness
Mockery
Envy
questions.correctAnswer: Sidq, or truthfulness
questions.explanation: Sidq means truthfulness in speech and action, even when honesty is difficult.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply Islamic values of truthfulness to school situations.

questions.prompt: Which example best shows Islamic teaching on fair trade in a school enterprise activity?
options: Using honest measures and clear prices
Hiding faults in products
Changing prices after payment secretly
Keeping group money without records
questions.correctAnswer: Using honest measures and clear prices
questions.explanation: Fair trade requires honesty, transparency, and avoiding harm or deception.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply Islamic guidance on fairness in transactions.

questions.prompt: Which question best analyses whether a charity collection follows Islamic ethics?
options: Were donations collected honestly, recorded clearly, and delivered to the intended people?
Did collectors hide the records?
Did one learner keep the money privately?
Were people in need publicly shamed?
questions.correctAnswer: Were donations collected honestly, recorded clearly, and delivered to the intended people?
questions.explanation: Ethical charity protects trust, dignity, accountability, and the rights of recipients.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze charitable activities using Islamic values of honesty and dignity.

questions.prompt: A group is studying Islamic heritage in Kenya. Which source would give the most reliable information?
options: A history text or knowledgeable teacher using verifiable evidence
Anonymous insults on social media
A rumour from a class chat
A joke made during break time
questions.correctAnswer: A history text or knowledgeable teacher using verifiable evidence
questions.explanation: Responsible study of heritage uses accurate sources and avoids stereotypes or rumours.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze reliable sources for learning about Islamic heritage.

questions.prompt: Which project best applies Islamic values to digital conduct?
options: Create class guidelines on truthful sharing, privacy, modest speech, and reporting harm
Forward messages before checking them
Use anonymous accounts to insult classmates
Share private photos without permission
questions.correctAnswer: Create class guidelines on truthful sharing, privacy, modest speech, and reporting harm
questions.explanation: Islamic values support truthful, respectful, private, and responsible communication online.
questions.learningOutcome: Create digital conduct guidelines informed by Islamic moral values.

questions.prompt: In Hindu Religious Education, what does dharma broadly refer to?
options: Righteous duty and moral order
Careless speech
A school bus route
Avoiding all responsibility
questions.correctAnswer: Righteous duty and moral order
questions.explanation: Dharma guides right conduct, duty, harmony, and responsibility in personal and social life.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe dharma as a guide to duty and right conduct.

questions.prompt: What does ahimsa mainly encourage in Hindu teaching?
options: Non-violence and respect for life
Revenge after disagreement
Careless harm to living beings
Mockery of weak people
questions.correctAnswer: Non-violence and respect for life
questions.explanation: Ahimsa encourages avoiding harm in thought, word, and action where possible.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify ahimsa as a value that promotes non-violence and care for life.

questions.prompt: Which action best applies ahimsa in a school conflict?
options: Use calm words and seek mediation instead of fighting
Reply to insults with violence
Encourage classmates to attack
Destroy another learner's property
questions.correctAnswer: Use calm words and seek mediation instead of fighting
questions.explanation: Ahimsa supports peaceful responses that avoid harm and seek respectful resolution.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply ahimsa to peaceful conflict resolution.

questions.prompt: Which statement best explains karma as a moral idea in Hindu teaching?
options: Actions have consequences and people should act responsibly
Actions never matter
Only public actions count
Responsibility belongs only to adults
questions.correctAnswer: Actions have consequences and people should act responsibly
questions.explanation: Karma encourages awareness that choices shape personal and social outcomes.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain karma as a reason for responsible moral conduct.

questions.prompt: What is seva in many Hindu communities?
options: Selfless service offered for the good of others
A way to avoid community duty
A private insult
A school punishment
questions.correctAnswer: Selfless service offered for the good of others
questions.explanation: Seva encourages service without selfish gain and supports compassion and community welfare.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe seva as selfless service and apply it to community life.

questions.prompt: A learner wants to practise seva in the neighbourhood. Which activity fits best?
options: Join a clean-up and help elderly neighbours without seeking praise
Record a fake service activity
Demand payment before every kind action
Refuse to help unless friends are watching
questions.correctAnswer: Join a clean-up and help elderly neighbours without seeking praise
questions.explanation: Seva emphasizes sincere service that benefits others and builds community wellbeing.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply seva through practical community service.

questions.prompt: Which practice in Hindu tradition is commonly linked with discipline, meditation, and self-control?
options: Yoga
Zakat
Baptism
Salah
questions.correctAnswer: Yoga
questions.explanation: Yoga can involve disciplined practice, meditation, self-control, and spiritual reflection.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify yoga as a practice linked to discipline and self-control.

questions.prompt: Which question best analyses whether a choice follows dharma?
options: Does it fulfil duty while protecting truth, fairness, and harmony?
Does it make me famous quickly?
Can it hide harm from others?
Will it excuse laziness?
questions.correctAnswer: Does it fulfil duty while protecting truth, fairness, and harmony?
questions.explanation: Dharma-based reflection considers duty, right conduct, truth, fairness, and social harmony.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze moral choices using dharma and responsibility.

questions.prompt: A learner studies Diwali as a Hindu festival. Which focus shows deeper understanding?
options: Explaining its values of light, renewal, family, and moral reflection
Counting decorations without meaning
Using the festival to mock another religion
Avoiding any question about values
questions.correctAnswer: Explaining its values of light, renewal, family, and moral reflection
questions.explanation: Religious festivals should be understood through the beliefs and values they express.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze values expressed through Hindu festivals.

questions.prompt: Which plan best helps Grade 9 learners apply Hindu values to environmental care?
options: Create a project on ahimsa, responsible use of resources, tree care, and reflection
Hold one talk and continue wasting resources
Burn plastic near classrooms
Dump waste into a stream secretly
questions.correctAnswer: Create a project on ahimsa, responsible use of resources, tree care, and reflection
questions.explanation: A strong plan links values with practical action, accountability, and reflection.
questions.learningOutcome: Create environmental care projects informed by Hindu values.

questions.prompt: Which value is most directly shown by admitting a mistake and asking for forgiveness?
options: Repentance
Arrogance
Revenge
Dishonesty
questions.correctAnswer: Repentance
questions.explanation: Repentance includes admitting wrong, seeking forgiveness, and choosing a better path.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify repentance as a step toward moral growth.

questions.prompt: What is self-control?
options: The ability to manage feelings, words, and actions responsibly
Doing anything one wants immediately
Blaming others for every mistake
Avoiding all advice from trusted adults
questions.correctAnswer: The ability to manage feelings, words, and actions responsibly
questions.explanation: Self-control helps a learner pause, think, and choose actions that respect values and other people.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe self-control as a value for responsible living.

questions.prompt: A learner is angry after being corrected. Which response best shows self-control?
options: Pause, listen, and respond respectfully after calming down
Shout insults immediately
Spread rumours about the teacher
Break another learner's property
questions.correctAnswer: Pause, listen, and respond respectfully after calming down
questions.explanation: Self-control creates space for respectful words and prevents harmful reactions.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply self-control in emotionally difficult situations.

questions.prompt: Which action best shows gratitude?
options: Thanking people and using their support responsibly
Complaining about every act of kindness
Taking gifts as if they are deserved
Ignoring everyone who helps
questions.correctAnswer: Thanking people and using their support responsibly
questions.explanation: Gratitude recognizes kindness and responds with appreciation and responsible use of help received.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify actions that show gratitude in daily life.

questions.prompt: Which habit best supports spiritual and moral growth?
options: Regular reflection on actions and willingness to improve
Avoiding all feedback
Repeating mistakes without concern
Judging others without self-examination
questions.correctAnswer: Regular reflection on actions and willingness to improve
questions.explanation: Reflection helps learners connect beliefs, values, behaviour, and personal improvement.
questions.learningOutcome: Use reflection to support spiritual and moral growth.

questions.prompt: A learner wants to apologize after spreading a false story. Which apology is most complete?
options: Admit the lie, apologize, correct the false story, and avoid repeating it
Say sorry but continue spreading the story
Blame everyone else for believing it
Apologize only if a teacher is watching
questions.correctAnswer: Admit the lie, apologize, correct the false story, and avoid repeating it
questions.explanation: A complete apology includes truth, remorse, repair, and a change in behaviour.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply practical steps for restoring trust after wrongdoing.

questions.prompt: Which choice best shows resilience guided by faith and values?
options: Seeking support, learning from failure, and continuing to do what is right
Giving up every duty after one mistake
Hiding problems through dishonesty
Hurting others because one feels disappointed
questions.correctAnswer: Seeking support, learning from failure, and continuing to do what is right
questions.explanation: Resilience helps a learner recover from difficulty while staying committed to responsible choices.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply resilience when facing challenges and moral pressure.

questions.prompt: Which response best supports a grieving classmate?
options: Listen kindly and connect the classmate with trusted support
Tell the classmate to stop feeling sad immediately
Share the classmate's story without permission
Avoid the classmate until they seem cheerful
questions.correctAnswer: Listen kindly and connect the classmate with trusted support
questions.explanation: Compassionate support respects feelings, privacy, and the need for trusted guidance.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze caring responses to people facing grief or difficulty.

questions.prompt: Which plan best helps a learner resist repeated pressure to join cheating?
options: Prepare a firm response, sit away from pressure, seek support, and study honestly
Promise to cheat only once
Avoid studying and depend on classmates
Blame the teacher for setting tests
questions.correctAnswer: Prepare a firm response, sit away from pressure, seek support, and study honestly
questions.explanation: A practical plan combines moral courage, boundaries, support, and responsible preparation.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze strategies for resisting peer pressure and choosing honest conduct.

questions.prompt: A peer-support club wants to promote respectful friendships. Which activity is best?
options: Create guidelines on consent, truthful speech, boundaries, and seeking help
Encourage learners to share private secrets
Reward insults called jokes
Ignore signs of bullying
questions.correctAnswer: Create guidelines on consent, truthful speech, boundaries, and seeking help
questions.explanation: Healthy relationships require respect, honesty, clear boundaries, safety, and trusted support.
questions.learningOutcome: Create guidelines for respectful and safe relationships.

questions.prompt: What is stewardship?
options: Responsible care for resources, creation, and duties entrusted to people
Using resources carelessly
Avoiding every responsibility
Keeping all benefits for oneself
questions.correctAnswer: Responsible care for resources, creation, and duties entrusted to people
questions.explanation: Stewardship means managing what one has responsibly for the good of people and creation.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe stewardship as responsible care for resources and creation.

questions.prompt: Which value is most important when handling money collected for a class charity activity?
options: Accountability
Secrecy
Wastefulness
Pride
questions.correctAnswer: Accountability
questions.explanation: Accountability requires honest records, responsible use, and clear reporting of shared resources.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify accountability as a value for handling shared resources.

questions.prompt: Which waste management choice best protects health and creation?
options: Dispose of waste safely and reuse or recycle where possible
Dump waste into rivers
Burn plastic near classrooms
Leave broken glass on the field
questions.correctAnswer: Dispose of waste safely and reuse or recycle where possible
questions.explanation: Safe disposal and reuse reduce harm to people, animals, soil, and water.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose practices that protect health and the environment.

questions.prompt: Why should learners care for animals and plants from a religious values perspective?
options: They are part of creation and should be treated responsibly
They exist only for careless amusement
Kindness to living things has no value
Cruelty proves courage
questions.correctAnswer: They are part of creation and should be treated responsibly
questions.explanation: Many religious teachings encourage care for living things and responsible use of the environment.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain why religious values support care for living things.

questions.prompt: A school tree-planting day fails because seedlings are not watered. Which reflection is most useful?
options: Find why care failed and create a watering and protection schedule
Stop all environmental work forever
Blame learners without checking facts
Plant more seedlings without changing anything
questions.correctAnswer: Find why care failed and create a watering and protection schedule
questions.explanation: Reflection should lead to better planning, shared responsibility, and practical improvement.
questions.learningOutcome: Improve stewardship projects through reflection and planning.

questions.prompt: A learner wants to use pocket money responsibly. Which plan best reflects stewardship?
options: Budget for needs, save some money, and share where possible
Spend everything immediately on wants
Borrow without planning to repay
Hide spending from guardians
questions.correctAnswer: Budget for needs, save some money, and share where possible
questions.explanation: Stewardship of money includes planning, self-control, honesty, and generosity.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply stewardship values to personal financial choices.

questions.prompt: Which action best shows responsibility in a group service project?
options: Complete assigned duties and report progress honestly
Claim credit for work done by others
Hide unused supplies at home
Ignore safety rules
questions.correctAnswer: Complete assigned duties and report progress honestly
questions.explanation: Responsible service includes doing one's part, being honest, and caring for shared resources.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply responsibility and honesty in group service.

questions.prompt: Which question best evaluates an environmental project from a religious values perspective?
options: Does it protect life, use resources wisely, and involve the community fairly?
Does it make one learner famous?
Can it hide pollution from visitors?
Will it avoid all cooperation?
questions.correctAnswer: Does it protect life, use resources wisely, and involve the community fairly?
questions.explanation: A values-based evaluation considers care for life, responsible resource use, fairness, and participation.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze stewardship projects using religious and moral values.

questions.prompt: A group collects food for families in need. Which practice best protects dignity?
options: Distribute support privately and respectfully through trusted channels
Announce names to embarrass recipients
Keep the best items for organisers
Use donations to reward friends only
questions.correctAnswer: Distribute support privately and respectfully through trusted channels
questions.explanation: Service should meet needs while protecting privacy, fairness, and human dignity.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze ways to protect dignity during service activities.

questions.prompt: Which plan best shows a Grade 9 class practising stewardship for one term?
options: Assign teams to save water, track waste, care for plants, and review progress weekly
Hold one speech and take no action
Collect money without records
Punish anyone who asks questions
questions.correctAnswer: Assign teams to save water, track waste, care for plants, and review progress weekly
questions.explanation: A strong stewardship plan has clear duties, evidence, accountability, and regular reflection.
questions.learningOutcome: Create practical stewardship action plans for school life.

questions.prompt: What is cyberbullying?
options: Using digital tools to threaten, shame, or harass someone
Submitting homework online
Reading an e-book quietly
Joining a respectful class chat
questions.correctAnswer: Using digital tools to threaten, shame, or harass someone
questions.explanation: Cyberbullying harms dignity and safety by using phones, computers, or online spaces to mistreat others.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify harmful digital behavior and its moral impact.

questions.prompt: Which value is most important when settling a conflict peacefully?
options: Justice
Revenge
Hatred
Dishonesty
questions.correctAnswer: Justice
questions.explanation: Justice helps people seek fairness, truth, and restoration instead of revenge.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify values that support peaceful conflict resolution.

questions.prompt: Which online action best reflects religious values of respect and truth?
options: Verify information before sharing and avoid insulting comments
Forward rumours to become popular
Use anonymous accounts to mock others
Share private photos without permission
questions.correctAnswer: Verify information before sharing and avoid insulting comments
questions.explanation: Digital responsibility requires truthfulness, respect, privacy, and care for the effect of messages.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply religious values to responsible use of digital media.

questions.prompt: Why is forgiveness important for peace?
options: It can reduce revenge and open a path to restored relationships
It means pretending harm never happened
It allows wrong actions to continue without change
It removes the need for justice
questions.correctAnswer: It can reduce revenge and open a path to restored relationships
questions.explanation: Forgiveness supports peace when combined with truth, responsibility, and efforts to make things right.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how forgiveness can contribute to peace and reconciliation.

questions.prompt: A class chat has started spreading insults about a learner's religion. What should a responsible learner do?
options: Refuse to join, save evidence if needed, and report to a trusted adult
Add more insults to look brave
Forward the messages to more groups
Tell the victim to remain silent forever
questions.correctAnswer: Refuse to join, save evidence if needed, and report to a trusted adult
questions.explanation: Responsible action protects the targeted learner and helps stop harmful digital behaviour.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safe and responsible responses to online harassment.

questions.prompt: Which action is most likely to reduce conflict between two classmates?
options: Listening to both sides before agreeing on a fair solution
Spreading one-sided rumours
Encouraging the conflict to continue
Refusing any apology
questions.correctAnswer: Listening to both sides before agreeing on a fair solution
questions.explanation: Peaceful conflict resolution requires listening, fairness, and willingness to repair relationships.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply listening and fairness to resolve conflict.

questions.prompt: Which example shows discrimination based on religion?
options: Refusing to include a learner in a group because of their faith
Sharing class notes with everyone
Asking a respectful question about a festival
Working together on a clean-up project
questions.correctAnswer: Refusing to include a learner in a group because of their faith
questions.explanation: Discrimination treats a person unfairly because of identity or belief and harms dignity.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognize discrimination and choose inclusive actions.

questions.prompt: Which question best tests whether a peace plan is fair?
options: Does it listen to affected people and address the real cause of conflict?
Does it silence the weakest person?
Does it hide all facts from the group?
Does it reward harm without repair?
questions.correctAnswer: Does it listen to affected people and address the real cause of conflict?
questions.explanation: A fair peace plan considers truth, affected people, causes, responsibility, and practical repair.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate peacebuilding plans using fairness and responsibility.

questions.prompt: Which question is best before sharing a religious message online?
options: Is it true, respectful, necessary, and safe to share?
Will it embarrass someone quickly?
Can it make me popular even if false?
Will it start conflict between groups?
questions.correctAnswer: Is it true, respectful, necessary, and safe to share?
questions.explanation: A responsible learner checks truth, respect, purpose, and possible harm before sharing digital content.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze digital messages using religious values and responsible citizenship.

questions.prompt: A school wants rules for respectful online learning. Which rule is strongest?
options: Use truthful words, protect privacy, report harm, and disagree respectfully
Post private images whenever classmates annoy you
Forward any message before checking it
Allow insults if they are called jokes
questions.correctAnswer: Use truthful words, protect privacy, report harm, and disagree respectfully
questions.explanation: Strong digital rules protect truth, dignity, privacy, safety, and peaceful communication.
questions.learningOutcome: Create digital conduct guidelines based on religious and moral values.

questions.prompt: What is interfaith dialogue?
options: Respectful conversation among people of different faiths to build understanding
A debate meant to humiliate another religion
A rule that no one may explain their beliefs
A way to spread rumours about worship practices
questions.correctAnswer: Respectful conversation among people of different faiths to build understanding
questions.explanation: Interfaith dialogue encourages listening, accurate understanding, and peaceful relationships among communities.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe interfaith dialogue as a way of promoting understanding and peace.

questions.prompt: Which value best supports national cohesion in a religiously diverse country?
options: Respect
Hatred
Mockery
Exclusion
questions.correctAnswer: Respect
questions.explanation: Respect helps citizens live peacefully with people whose backgrounds and beliefs differ from theirs.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify values that support national cohesion and peaceful coexistence.

questions.prompt: Which action would best promote inclusion during a school cultural and religious day?
options: Allow groups to share approved presentations respectfully and safely
Invite only one group and exclude the rest
Permit jokes that insult minority traditions
Cancel questions from learners who want to understand
questions.correctAnswer: Allow groups to share approved presentations respectfully and safely
questions.explanation: Inclusive events provide fair opportunities for learning while maintaining respect and safety.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply inclusive practices in school activities involving different faiths.

questions.prompt: Why should stereotypes about religious communities be avoided?
options: They can spread false ideas and lead to unfair treatment
They always help people understand accurately
They are the best source for learning
They make respectful dialogue unnecessary
questions.correctAnswer: They can spread false ideas and lead to unfair treatment
questions.explanation: Stereotypes reduce people to unfair labels and can damage trust, dignity, and peace.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain why stereotypes harm interfaith relations and social cohesion.

questions.prompt: A rumour is causing tension between two faith clubs. Which step is most ethical?
options: Check facts with responsible leaders before making accusations
Punish one club without listening
Share the rumour more widely
Let anger decide what happened
questions.correctAnswer: Check facts with responsible leaders before making accusations
questions.explanation: Ethical investigation protects truth, fairness, and the dignity of all people involved.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply truthfulness and fairness to prevent interfaith conflict.

questions.prompt: Which shared activity is most likely to strengthen friendship between different faith groups?
options: A community clean-up followed by respectful reflection on shared values
A contest to prove one group is superior
A campaign to avoid all contact
A meeting where only one group may speak
questions.correctAnswer: A community clean-up followed by respectful reflection on shared values
questions.explanation: Shared service allows groups to cooperate around common values such as care, responsibility, and peace.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply shared service as a way of building interfaith understanding.

questions.prompt: Which question best evaluates whether an interfaith event was successful?
options: Did participants learn accurately, feel respected, and agree on positive next steps?
Did one group silence everyone else?
Did the event create new rumours?
Did learners leave with more stereotypes?
questions.correctAnswer: Did participants learn accurately, feel respected, and agree on positive next steps?
questions.explanation: A successful interfaith event should build knowledge, respect, trust, and practical cooperation.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze interfaith activities using respect, accuracy, and cooperation.

questions.prompt: Which response best protects freedom of worship and classroom order?
options: Allow respectful religious expression while following school rules and respecting others
Allow one learner to disrupt everyone else
Ban all respectful mention of religion
Let learners insult beliefs they dislike
questions.correctAnswer: Allow respectful religious expression while following school rules and respecting others
questions.explanation: Freedom of worship works with responsibility, respect, and agreed rules for a peaceful school community.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze how religious freedom and responsibility can support peaceful coexistence.

questions.prompt: Which plan best prepares learners for a respectful visit to different places of worship?
options: Learn expected conduct, seek permission, prepare questions, and reflect on shared values
Arrive without permission and interrupt worship
Touch sacred objects to test reactions
Write jokes about every unfamiliar practice
questions.correctAnswer: Learn expected conduct, seek permission, prepare questions, and reflect on shared values
questions.explanation: Preparation helps learners observe respectfully, ask informed questions, and connect learning with values.
questions.learningOutcome: Create respectful plans for learning from different places of worship.

questions.prompt: A Grade 9 class wants to promote unity before transition to Senior School. Which campaign best reflects Religious Education values?
options: A campaign on respect, truthful speech, shared service, and peaceful conflict resolution
A campaign ranking religions from best to worst
A campaign encouraging learners to avoid those with different beliefs
A campaign spreading jokes about worship practices
questions.correctAnswer: A campaign on respect, truthful speech, shared service, and peaceful conflict resolution
questions.explanation: Religious Education values support unity through respect, truth, service, justice, and peace.
questions.learningOutcome: Create school campaigns that promote unity through religious and moral values.
